insight.title: How Curiosity Rebuilds the World
insight.subtitle: The quiet art of turning today’s questions into tomorrow’s tools.

sections.text: We are born with a restless desire to improve the tools we hold. It begins as a quiet itch, a tiny whisper asking if a stone could be sharper or a light brighter. This is the seed of change. We don't just inhabit the world; we are constantly reimagining its very foundation.

Innovation happens when an old problem meets a fresh pair of eyes. It is the art of rearranging the familiar into something entirely new. Like a weaver pulling threads, we combine ancient wisdom with modern craft. We take the rhythm of the tides and turn it into warmth for our homes.

This endless cycle of making makes our lives softer and our horizons wider. Every new breakthrough is a gift from the present to the future. It is how we speak to generations we will never meet. We build bridges and craft stories, ensuring that the path ahead is always a little clearer.

news.title: Dal researchers earn prestigious national CIHR career awards for breakthrough health research
news.description: Two Dalhousie medical researchers earned major career awards, highlighting their work in immune regulation and transformative health‑care delivery that is shaping future treatments and improving patient outcomes.

news.title: Cannabis compounds CBD and CBG may help reverse fatty liver disease, study finds
news.description: CBD and CBG, two non-intoxicating cannabis compounds, may help combat fatty liver disease by boosting liver energy reserves and restoring cellular cleanup systems. In the study, both compounds improved blood sugar control and reduced harmful lipids linked to fatty liver disease. Researchers say the findings point to a promising new plant-based approach to treating metabolic liver disorders.

news.title: A thousand anomalies hiding in plain sight
news.description: Systematic human inspection of the millions of source cutouts in the Hubble Legacy Archive is impossible – but artificial intelligence has now uncovered more than a thousand astrophysical anomalies hiding in plain sight.

news.title: Psychology says mothers who can identify their son's mood from the way he says "hello" on the phone have developed these 6 attunement patterns
news.description: Scientists have discovered that mothers who can instantly decode their son's emotional state from just two words on the phone have developed a neurological connection so profound that it triggers the same hormonal response as a physical hug—creating a bond that research shows will never be matched by any romantic partner, friend, or therapist in his lifetime.
